extraction.name: Vibravox
extraction.description: Vibravox is a dataset compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) containing audio recordings using five different body-conduction audio sensors: two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone. The dataset also includes audio data from an airborne microphone used as a reference.
extraction.creator: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poirée, Véronique Zimpfer, and Éric Bavu
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The recording process consists of four steps performed consecutively for each participant: 1) speech-clean (reading sentences for 15 minutes), 2) speechless-noisy (remaining silent in a noisy environment for 2 minutes and 24 seconds), 3) speechless-clean (remaining silent in complete silence for 54 seconds), and 4) speech-noisy (reading sentences in a noisy environment for 54 seconds).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: A small number of audio clips had shortcomings such as mispronounced sentences, sensors shifting from their initial positions, occasional sensor malfunctions, or instances where a microphone was inadvertently left unequipped, leading to data inconsistencies.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Audio recordings using five different body-conduction audio sensors and an airborne reference microphone. The text utilized for participant readings originates from the French Wikipedia subset of Common Voice.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: A 20 Hz high-pass filter is uniformly applied to each acquisition channel. Timestamps generated by Voice Activity Detection (VAD) are extended by 0.6 seconds on both sides, and in rare cases trimmed by 15 ms to eliminate unwanted artifacts.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A series of three automatic filters were applied to remove utterances with obvious deficiencies. The filters discarded samples with a Phoneme Error Rate > 10%, verified sensor functionality using the ratio between speech and silence energy levels, and detected potential sensitivity drift.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Phonetic transcriptions were generated using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) via a text phonemizer. A phase of manual phonetic transcription was then necessary for unrecognized words.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Textual filters were applied to exclude most proper names, retaining only common first names, French town or region names, and country names. Utterances containing numbers, Greek letters, mathematical symbols, or syntactic errors were carefully removed.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: text phonemizer of the CoML lab, whisper-timestamped model
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender (97 Female / 91 Male), voice biometrics, and physiological sounds (heart rate, breathing).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset offers potential for improving communication in noisy environments, developing voice commands, monitoring vital signs, access control, and intelligence gathering.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The speech-noisy subset primarily serves testing purposes, as it lacks a clean reference. In some cases, such as when a participant's ear canal was too small for the rigid in-ear microphone to achieve proper acoustic sealing, the automatic filters were not triggered.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing for speech enhancement (bandwidth extension), speech-to-phonemes recognition, and speaker verification.
